units.description: The number of characters (Unicode code points) in the UTF-8 text s. Count the bytes that are not continuation bytes: a continuation byte is one whose value is 128 to 191 inclusive. The empty text has 0 characters. Never panics.
tests: pub fn test_count_1() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_count("") == 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_count_2() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_count("abc") == 3); return 0; }
pub fn test_count_3() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_count("café") == 4); return 0; }
pub fn test_count_4() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_count("日本語") == 3); return 0; }
pub fn test_count_5() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_count("a日b") == 3); return 0; }

units.description: start is a byte index at the start of a character in s. Answer the byte index just past that character: the lead byte at start is followed by zero or more continuation bytes (128 to 191), and the answer is the index of the first byte after them, or len(s) if there is none. If start is at or beyond len(s), answer len(s). Never panics.

units.signature: fn editdistance_span_eq[&a, &b](a: &a [byte], a0: int, a1: int, b: &b [byte], b0: int, b1: int) -> [] bool
units.description: True when the byte range a[a0..a1] of a and the byte range b[b0..b1] of b hold exactly the same bytes, with the same length. Two empty ranges are equal. Ranges are byte indexes of whole characters as produced by editdistance_char_end. Never panics.
tests: pub fn test_span_eq_1() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("café", 3, 5, "café", 3, 5) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_span_eq_2() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("café", 3, 5, "cafe", 3, 4) == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_span_eq_3() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("abc", 0, 1, "xbc", 0, 1) == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_span_eq_4() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("abc", 1, 2, "xbc", 1, 2) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_span_eq_5() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("", 0, 0, "", 0, 0) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_span_eq_6() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_span_eq("ab", 0, 2, "a", 0, 1) == false); return 0; }

units.signature: fn edit_distance[&h, &a, &b](heap: &!h Heap, a: &a [byte], b: &b [byte]) -> [heap] int
units.description: The Levenshtein distance between the texts a and b: the fewest single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn a into b. Every length and position counts characters (code points), never bytes: "é" is one character, "日本語" is three. Use two rows of the dynamic-programming table (one row per character of a, sized by the character count of b), allocated from heap with box_slice and freed with unbox_slice before returning. Walk the characters of each text with editdistance_char_end, and compare characters with editdistance_span_eq. It must run quickly on strings of 60 characters, so no exponential recursion. Empty text is at distance len of the other. Result is always 0 or more, and 0 exactly when a equals b. Never panics on any bytes.
tests: pub fn test_edit_distance_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert(edit_distance(heap, "kitten", "sitting") == 3); return 0; }

units.signature: fn similarity_pct[&h, &a, &b](heap: &!h Heap, a: &a [byte], b: &b [byte]) -> [heap] int
units.description: A whole number from 0 to 100 measuring how alike a and b are. If both texts are empty the answer is 100. Otherwise let m be the character count of the longer text (characters, never bytes) and d the edit_distance of a and b; the answer is (100 * (m - d)) divided by m, using integer division that rounds down. The answer is always between 0 and 100. Never panics.

units.signature: fn closest[&h, &q, &l](heap: &!h Heap, query: &q [byte], candidates: &l list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] option.Option[buffer.Buffer]
units.description: Among the texts in candidates, the one with the smallest edit_distance to query. If several candidates tie for the smallest distance, the one that comes first in the list wins. Answer Some with a new buffer holding a copy of the winning candidate's bytes, or None when candidates is empty. Walk the list by matching on it, compute each distance with edit_distance, and keep the best so far. Never panics.
tests: fn cases_closest_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }
fn cases_closest_mk[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, s: &r [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]] { let b = box_slice(heap, len(s), byte_of(0)); borrow mut b as &!w in { copy_into(contents(w), s); } return b; }

fn cases_closest_ldrop[&h](heap: &!h Heap, l: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] int { match l { list.List::Empty => { return 0; } list.List::Cons(f, rest) => { unbox_slice(heap, unbox(heap, f)); let tail = unbox(heap, rest); return 1 + cases_closest_ldrop(heap, tail); } } }

fn cases_closest_some[&h, &t1, &l2, &w](heap: &!h Heap, a1: &t1 [byte], a2: &l2 list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]], want: &w [byte]) -> [heap] int { match closest(heap, a1, a2) { option.Option::Some(v) => { var same = false; borrow v as &x in { same = cases_closest_same(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, v); if same { return 0; } return 1; } option.Option::None => { return 2; } } }

fn cases_closest_none[&h, &t1, &l2](heap: &!h Heap, a1: &t1 [byte], a2: &l2 list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]]) -> [heap] int { match closest(heap, a1, a2) { option.Option::Some(v) => { buffer.drop(heap, v); return 2; } option.Option::None => { return 0; } } }

fn cases_closest_c1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var a2: list.List[Box[Box[[byte]]]] = list.List::Empty; a2 = list.push(heap, a2, box(heap, cases_closest_mk(heap, "abe"))); a2 = list.push(heap, a2, box(heap, cases_closest_mk(heap, "abd"))); var code = 1; borrow a2 as &ra2 in { code = cases_closest_some(heap, "abc", ra2, "abd"); } cases_closest_ldrop(heap, a2); return code; }
pub fn test_closest_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_closest_c1(heap), 0); return 0; }
